dateline: Hawthorne, CA / Boca Chica, TX — May 2002–Present
heroHeadline: June 2: T-2 to IPO Roadshow — Starlink 12-26 Scrubbed; $6.45B Space Force Week; S-1/A on SEC EDGAR
heroSubtitle: 8,792 days since SpaceX founding — June 2, 2026 is T-2 before the historic IPO management roadshow begins June 4–8. The Starlink Group 12-26 Falcon 9 launch scrubbed from SLC-4E Vandenberg and was rescheduled to June 3, keeping the 2026 orbital mission count at 68. The S-1/A Amendment filed June 1 became publicly visible on SEC EDGAR on June 2, disclosing that SpaceX is now redescribed as an 'AI services and infrastructure company' following the xAI merger, and revealing Elon Musk's ~1 billion performance-based restricted shares vesting across 15 tranches (market cap + Mars colony milestones); underwriters confirmed as Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, BofA, Citi, and JPMorgan. The previous week saw SpaceX close two landmark Space Force contracts totaling $6.45B: the $2.29B Space Data Network (SDN) Backbone (May 27, Starshield-based military SATCOM) and the $4.16B Space-Based Airborne Moving Target Indicator (SB-AMTI) constellation to track cruise missiles and hypersonic glide vehicles from LEO (May 29) — the largest single-week Space Force award total in company history. Starship remains grounded under FAA IFT-12 mishap investigation; Booster 20 + Ship 40 continue integration at Starbase for IFT-13 targeting July–August 2026. IPO pricing June 11, Nasdaq (SPCX) debut June 12, targeting a $75–80B raise at $1.75T–$2T+ valuation.
